content:
Using standard order of operations, insert exactly two \(+\ \) and two \(\div\).

A valid expression is:
\[
1+111\div 1\div 111+1
\]
This uses \(1+3+1+3+1=9\) ones and exactly two \(+\), two \(\div\).

Evaluate:
\[
1+111\div 1\div 111+1 = 1+(111\div 1\div 111)+1 = 1+1+1=3.
\]

No result \(1\) or \(2\) is possible: expressions with two standalone positive integer terms are already \(>2\), and expressions with one standalone integer plus two division terms would need those two fractions to sum to \(1\), but each proper repunit fraction is \(<1/10\), so their sum is \(<1/5\).

Thus the smallest possible integer is \(\boxed{3}\).
